html:
SMTO-BOOT-0011 — The program that runs the AI model wasn't found

GUID: 51675c22-fdb7-45cd-b9dc-05960c910249
Slug: boot-model-server-missing
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The model start script couldn't find the model engine program it launches (llama-server, Ollama or vLLM), or the curl tool it uses for checks. It stopped before starting the model, so nothing was loaded.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the terminal message: it shows the path where the script looked for the engine program, or says which tool is missing. Scripts look in a fixed default place, so an engine installed elsewhere isn't found.
  2. If the engine isn't installed yet, set it up first: build llama.cpp (src/llama/setup.sh shows how), install Ollama, or run src/vllm/install-vllm.sh for vLLM. The start scripts only launch an engine; they don't install one.
  3. If it's installed somewhere else, set the matching option before the command: SERVER_BIN or LLAMA_SERVER_BIN for llama.cpp, OLLAMA_BIN for Ollama, or VLLM_BIN for vLLM. These options point the script at the exact program to run.
  4. For Ollama scripts, also install curl. Before starting again, check that no model engine is already running on the same port. Ollama scripts use curl to check the engine is ready, and a second copy would compete for the graphics cards.

What success looks like

  • The script gets past its checks and the model engine starts loading the model.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the Error reference line, and send it to the person who maintains the model setup. Remove passwords, tokens and private folder names before sharing it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A model launcher could not resolve or execute its server binary (llama-server via SERVER_BIN or LLAMA_SERVER_BIN, ollama via OLLAMA_BIN, vllm via VLLM_BIN) or could not find curl for the Ollama health check, and exited before starting the server.

What this means

  • Model-launch scripts fail to resolve or execute the selected llama-server/Ollama/vLLM binary, or lack curl required by the Ollama health-check path. The selected launcher stops before starting its model server. Executable lookup does not verify that the installed build supports the model. A missing executable does not establish whether the package is absent, its path is wrong, or file permissions prevent execution.

Why this can happen

  • Model-launch scripts fail to resolve or execute the selected llama-server/Ollama/vLLM binary, or lack curl required by the Ollama health-check path.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the exact missing executable and the selected launcher's path variable before installing a different engine.

How to fix it

  • Verify the path named in the error is an executable (ls -l, command -v), build or install the engine (src/llama/setup.sh for llama.cpp, Ollama, or src/vllm/install-vllm.sh), and export the launcher's binary variable (SERVER_BIN, LLAMA_SERVER_BIN, OLLAMA_BIN or VLLM_BIN) to it; install curl for the Ollama launchers. Check for an already-running server on the target port before launching another instance.
  • Install the named required executable and set the selected launcher's supported binary-path option, such as SERVER_BIN, LLAMA_SERVER_BIN, OLLAMA_BIN or VLLM_BIN.

Retry and execution caution

  • Resolve the named executable through the selected launcher's binary-path option; inspect existing servers before starting another instance.

How to verify the fix

  • The launcher resolves its intended server and required health-check tools.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The selected launcher stops before starting its model server. Executable lookup does not verify that the installed build supports the model.
  • A missing executable does not establish whether the package is absent, its path is wrong, or file permissions prevent execution.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
